final_recommendation: The room converged on a unified binding dispute panel covering wage floor, RVC, and tariff classification with automatic 25% duties and 90-day resolution. Canada accepted 2.5% annual dairy TRQ growth. The sunset clause remains unresolved despite repeated business warnings about investment freezes.
minority_objections: supply_chain_mfr repeatedly warned that unresolved sunset clause would freeze cross-border capex and kill ratification, but was ignored by negotiators focused on autos and dairy
dairy_ag initially pushed for 3.6% TRQ growth but was overruled by the 2.5% compromise that kept Canada in the room
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada's initial red line vs. USTR's absolute refusal, resolved by creating expedited auto panel as substitute mechanism
Dairy access: U.S. agriculture demanded 3.6% TRQ growth vs. Canada's defense of supply management, settled at 2.5% annual growth
Enforcement scope: labor_union demanded unified panel vs. initial proposals for separate labor/auto tracks, resolved by single 90-day automatic-duty mechanism
key_concessions: Canada: abandoned Chapter 19 in exchange for binding auto panel with automatic enforcement; accepted 2.5% annual dairy TRQ growth
USTR: moved from bilateral-only threat to trilateral package by offering binding dispute panel as Chapter 19 substitute
Mexico: accepted unified North American wage floor (no separate Mexican indexing) and supported Canada's 2.5% dairy compromise
U.S. agriculture: accepted 2.5% instead of demanded 3.6% dairy TRQ growth to preserve trilateral deal
red_lines: Canada (initial): Chapter 19 and supply management non-negotiable; later traded Chapter 19 for binding auto panel
USTR: no Chapter 19 carve-out for Canada; Mexico's terms must be matched
labor_union: unilateral inspection authority and automatic tariff triggers; unified enforcement mechanism across all disputes
us_congress: no bilateral that excludes Canada (ratification killer); enforcement must have real teeth
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause / deal termination: supply_chain_mfr raised investment-freeze risk three times with explicit ratification warning, never answered by USTR or negotiators
Phase-in implementation details: auto_industry asked whether stagger applied to all vehicle classes; partially answered but cross-class compliance math left unclear
Dairy enforcement scope: Canada asked if binding panel covers dairy access disputes or only autos; question raised but not definitively resolved in transcript
downstream_risk_variables: Sunset clause renewal mechanism remains undefined; business warned this blocks cross-border investment
Dairy panel jurisdiction unclear: does binding dispute mechanism cover dairy access challenges or only auto-related disputes?
Implementation timeline coordination: stagger mechanics (sedans month 18, trucks month 20) agreed but cross-class compliance verification process not specified
Wage floor indexing: unified North American floor agreed but annual adjustment mechanism and dispute resolution for wage-level changes not detailed
uncertainty_notes: Sunset clause completely unresolved despite three explicit warnings it would kill ratification. Dairy dispute jurisdiction ambiguous—Canada asked if binding panel covers dairy access challenges but received no clear answer. Cross-class auto phase-in stagger agreed in principle but verification/compliance process for different vehicle classes not specified.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: Auto RVC/labor-value drove 5 rounds of negotiation; stagger mechanism (sedans month 18, trucks month 20) and unified wage floor were the concrete breakthroughs that unlocked the package
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: labor_union and us_congress made unilateral inspection authority and automatic tariff triggers a ratification prerequisite; unified 90-day panel with 25% duties was the deal-making concession
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's initial red line on supply management; 2.5% annual TRQ growth was the specific compromise that kept Canada in the trilateral (Mexico proposed it, Canada accepted, dairy_ag conceded from 3.6%)
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada opened with 'Chapter 19 or we walk'; USTR's absolute refusal forced creation of binding auto panel with automatic duties as the substitute mechanism that closed the deal
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: supply_chain_mfr raised sunset/investment-freeze risk three times with explicit ratification warning, but no proposal or concession resulted—acknowledged as serious but not resolved
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: us_congress stated bilateral-only would be 'ratification killer' and forced trilateral structure; labor enforcement teeth and unified panel were shaped by Congressional vote-counting
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: auto_industry and supply_chain_mfr raised phase-in windows and compliance cost modeling as concerns; 18-month stagger was the response but did not drive the final outcome (autos/labor/dairy did)
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's 'match Mexico or watch us finalize bilateral' threat was the opening leverage; Canada's acceptance of 2.5% dairy and abandonment of Chapter 19 were direct responses to this pressure

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
